capabilities.text: Type or paste the data as a list of values, one dot per value with equal values stacked
Give the data as a frequency table: each value once with how many of it there are
capabilities.note: one row per value and count, with tab or CSV paste. The first two cells are used. Zero or blank counts extend the automatic range without adding marks or affecting mean or median. Each stack draws up to 100 marks, and the editor notes say so when a stack is cut short. Mean and median use the full counts. Switching forms fills an empty destination and preserves text already there. Converting to a list uses at most 5,000 entries. A multiline field replaces the reference’s separate table cells

capabilities.text: Use fractions and mixed numbers such as 3/4 and 1 1/2 as values, with the number line numbered in fractions
capabilities.note: fraction and mixed-number input with reduced stacked labels. The automatic fit uses a supported step that places every value on a tick within 24 intervals, or falls back to a rounded decimal range. Typing a fraction in a manual range field preserves its spelling and enables fractional tick labels where representable

capabilities.text: Give students a blank number line to plot the data on
capabilities.note: clearing data on a new plot draws an empty 0–10 number line or the manual range. A saved plot keeps its original drawing through ordinary edits. New options use the current layout, with the original tick phase for supported manual ranges

capabilities.text: Draw X's instead of dots as the marks
capabilities.note: X marks use the same stacks and hide on the student copy

capabilities.text: Write an axis title under the number line
Put a blank line in place of the chart or axis title for students
capabilities.note: both titles independently offer text, a writing line or none. Writing lines also draw on the student copy
turning the automatic line off is part of typing a range
5 to 12 is the automatic range for the opening data. This example changes the step to 0.5 within the same range

capabilities.text: Have the number line's range and count-by worked out from the data
capabilities.note: the opening already has data, so the render differs because the data changes; the checker confirms the axis is re-fitted

capabilities.text: Choose which ticks are numbered (every tick, every 2nd, 4th, 5th or 10th, or none)
capabilities.note: all six choices keep the ticks. Numbering is anchored at zero when present, otherwise at the first tick. At a maximum width of 880 SVG units, crowded labels thin by a regular multiple of the chosen stride. Thinning prefers 1, 2, 5 and powers-of-ten multiples of those, with quarter, half and whole subdivisions tried first on fractional lines. End ticks are numbered when they align with the resulting stride

capabilities.text: Finish an end of the number line with an arrow
capabilities.note: each end can use a triangle or line arrow. Plain ends remain the default for saved drawings

capabilities.text: Finish an end of the number line with a circle
capabilities.note: a filled circle can finish either end independently
